authoredSolutions.51: Note \(2\sin|x|\cos|x|=\sin(2|x|)\). For \(x\to0^+\), \(f(x)=a+x-\frac{\sin 2x}{x}\to a-2\). For \(x\to0^-\), \(f(x)=-a+x+\frac{\sin 2x}{x}\to -a+2\). Continuity needs \(a-2=-a+2\Rightarrow a=2\), and then \(b=\lim f=a-2=0\). Hence \(a+b=2\).
authoredSolutions.52: Grouping the terms, the expression equals \(\sin\left(\frac{15\theta}{2}-8\theta\right)+\cos\left(\frac{15\theta}{2}-8\theta\right)=\cos\frac{\theta}{2}-\sin\frac{\theta}{2}\). From \(\cot\theta=-\frac{1}{2\sqrt2}\) with \(\frac{\pi}{2}<\theta<\pi\): \(\sin\theta=\frac{2\sqrt2}{3}\). Now \(\left(\cos\frac\theta2-\sin\frac\theta2\right)^2=1-\sin\theta=\frac{3-2\sqrt2}{3}=\frac{(\sqrt2-1)^2}{3}\). Since \(\frac\theta2\in\left(\frac\pi4,\frac\pi2\right)\) the value is negative, so it equals \(\frac{1-\sqrt2}{\sqrt3}\).
